exceptions.reason: The row documents a native attribute that the React part does not read. In Vase UI the attribute goes to the element through the attributes, with its type from `HTMLAttributes`. A declared prop would take it out of the attributes.

surfaceAdditions.reason: The part reads `id` to give it to the root for `aria-labelledby`, so it is a declared prop. Base UI reads it from the native attributes of the label, and `types.md` has no row for a native attribute. The server HTML of the root differs from Base UI on purpose. A root that the consumer does not name assumes a label until it is mounted, so the server HTML points at the generated id. A label with no `id` prop has that id, so it names the root in the server HTML. Base UI gives the root an `aria-labelledby` only after the page hydrates. With no label, or with a label that has an `id` prop, no element has the generated id until the root is mounted. An `aria-labelledby` with no valid IDREF gives no name (step 2B of https://www.w3.org/TR/accname-1.2/#computation-steps), so the root then has the name that it has with no `aria-labelledby`. A root that has a non-blank `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` of the consumer has no generated id in the server HTML. The case "renders the generated id in the aria-labelledby of a root that has no label" in `ProgressRoot.node.test.tsx` asserts the server HTML. The case "renders no aria-labelledby of its own on a root that the consumer names: $name" asserts that a named root has no generated id. The case "has no aria-labelledby when it has no label" in `ProgressRoot.test.tsx` asserts that the mounted root has none.
